Clinton vs. Trump: A sweep by either =arty would likely rattle markets

=he current split in power. However, if Democrats keep the Presidency and take Senate or Republicans take =he

and =mplementation that will influence markets, which both parties, many individuals and circumstances will craft. This 
note =dentifies sectors, industries and stocks that we think would be price =ensitive to an unbalanced election outcome

Dividing issues: Taxes, trade, favored =nfrastructure types and monetary policy 
It's difficult to pin down specific =olicies from either candidate, but on several economic issues their =eneral bias is clear. 
These issues include taxes, trade deals, favored types of infrastructure — such as green vs =onventional energy, 
preference for monetary policy, and also their =xpressed views on industries such as Health Care and Energy. It is the 
=ist of the candidate's preference on these issues that we used to identify sectors and stocks sensitive to a sweep. 
Big banks might outperform small banks =nd oil might go down on Rep sweep 
While many of our conclusions align with =onventional judgment, we think we differ in that we think a Rep sweep =ould: 
1) be good for some domestic oil producers, as it should permit more drilling, but negative to the =ecovery in oil and gas 
prices, as more supply, and thus negative for =he broad Energy sector, 2) bring somewhat faster Fed hikes and a 
=tronger dollar than otherwise, 3) the first two could lead to lower inflation and a flatter yield curve than otherwise 
would =e. One could argue that Trump sized tax cuts and an infrastructure and =efense spending spree would steepen 
the curve, but we think this =nlikely while Republicans control the House. If Fed hikes bring yield curve flattening then 
big banks and capital =arkets likely outperform small banks and insurance companies. Slow =ikes that allow inflation to 
accelerate and steepen the curve might =avor smaller banks and insurance, but this could pressure PEs at non-financials. 
If the Fed falls too far behind the curve, =igher long-term rates could threaten the stock market, real estate and =he 
overall economy.

This week we're all about runways - the kind skinny models teeter on and the kind that planes race down. In honor of 
New York City's Fashion Week, starting September 8, we're showcasing hotels with interiors by superlative fashion 
designers, including Maison Moschino in Milan and Hotel Missoni in Edinburgh. Prefer hiking boots to high heels? We've 
got three Inkaterra properties in Peru, a secret destination in Bali, and an early ski sale in Aspen. So if you're looking for 
an adventure - fashionable or otherwise - we've got you covered. (Photo: Vivamarinha Hotel - Portugal - on sale Weds., 
Sept. 7)

London's Restored Belle-Epoque Beauty

Corinthia Hotel London is one of the latest luxury hotels to (re-)open in the soon-to-be Olympic capital. Fresh 
from a major restoration and refurbishment, the Belle Epoque property houses 294 rooms, some on two levels in 
rooftop turrets, and a David Collins-designed bar and restaurant. But the showstopper is Espa Life, a four-story "next-
generation" spa with an amphitheater sauna.

Serious hotel lovers across Asia think of this intimate refuge, in the shadow of holy Mount Agung, as a kind of 
secret handshake. Once you go, you're in the know, and most guests return to the black sand beachfront on Bali's less 
developed eastern shore every year. Designed by Kerry Hill of Aman Resorts fame, two thatch-roofed Balinese wantilans 
(meeting hall-style buildings) house 55 sleek but homey guestrooms, all with bijou balconies or patios overlooking 
coconut groves and the Indian Ocean.

Understated, Elegant Santa Barbara 
<http://cdn.jetsetter.com/statiatemplates/mktg/It-gray-pixel.gif> 
Bacara Resort -Santa Barbara 
<http://click.mailjetsetter.com/?qs=a643d7Sbcdf6125d7cbac665cbba91259ed0305eb86613154cOebOcb8218188c461e

Understated and elegant, with gorgeous beach views, Bacara Resort & Spa can be described in the same terms 
as Santa Barbara itself. The vibe across the property's 78 oceanside acres is sunny and sophisticated but entirely relaxed, 
encouraging guests to spend a day on the sand or in the spa. Large guestrooms come equipped with Frette linens and 
robes and are made for indulging indoors... but ocean views from the patio or balcony beckon.

A stay at Vivamarinha puts you close to Lisbon's cultural highlights (about 40 minutes away) as well as the 
beaches of the Portuguese Riviera in and around the pretty coastal town of Cascais. Rooms and suites are 
contemporary, spacious and of the settle-in-and-stay-a-while variety, with kitchen amenities, living areas and private 
outdoor spaces. Add to relaxation with a treatment in the world-class wellness area and on a walk through the 
manicured gardens.

Trendsetter on the Sunset Strip 
<http://cdn.jetsetter.com/statiatemplates/mktelt-gray-pixel.gif> 
Mondrian Los Angeles 
chttp://click.mail.jetsetter.com/?qs=6f8d2d077f2b317b2ce2279541276edb8f44cbce89c23cc4d23f928d4eb8bGee4lbce

One of the first hotels to define the Philippe Starck aesthetic, the Mondrian has gone from hectic L.A. hotspot to 
laid-back Sunset Boulevard classic. The bright minimalist feel of the original Starck design is intact, but since the hotel's 
2008 make-over, it feels a lot warmer and a little more relaxed, but just as chic. The views of L.A. are still unrivaled, and 
the scene at Skybar is hot; while you still might see someone famous at breakfast, it's more likely to be a confident 
leading lady than a striving supporting actress.

Alberta Ferretti's Italian Hideaway 
<http://cdn.jetsetter.com/static/templates/mktg/R-gray-pixelgif> 
Palazzo Viviani - Italy 
chttp://click.mailietsetter.com/?qs=97420dcbefd0d7867f422a69369600a3574ad59bc7926e09d4415d1db3edc2c1115c9

Atop a hill on the border of Italy's Romagna and Marche regions sits Castello di Montegridolfo, a lovingly 
restored medieval castle, converted to a romantic hotel. With an impressive artistic pedigree - it is part-owned by 
fashion designer Alberta Ferretti - the 54 suites scattered within its 14th century wheat-gold walls range from lush 
medievalism to dark-wood minimalism. But what sets the hotel apart are the striking views - order a sundown Negroni 
and watch the sky blush pink over the Adriatic.

Rasananda - Thailand 
<http://click.mail.jetsetter.com/?qs=10b9bf98cd738ebbfabelf4d281195fd2ea5eaa8932684e8efl6a04cc020982e5caee

Koh Phangan has a hedonistic reputation from its monthly Full Moon Parties, beloved by backpackers and gap-
year youngsters. But the Rasananda, on the opposite side of the island, is pure Thai class. Known for its intimate size and 
attentive staff, the resort is made up of 44 villas and suites, each with a private pool. The resort matches the 
surrounding area's natural beauty without being overbearing: The spa's teakwood treatment rooms are disguised in the 
jungle's fauna; the signature bistro serves locally inspired dishes al fresco. Taken all together, it's an escape to island 
paradise.
